summary.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue hit a record INR80.54 bn (+8.1% YoY) but EBITDA margin fell ~250 bps YoY to 11.7%, with FY27 targeting early double-digit margins.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 was LG Electronics India's highest-ever quarterly revenue at INR80.54 bn, up 8.1% YoY, with EBITDA of INR9.45 bn (11.7% margin) and PAT of INR6.93 bn (8.5%). Year-on-year margin compression was attributed to channel promotion spend (~1.1 pp), rupee depreciation (~5.6% YoY, ~1 pp impact), and e-waste compliance cost (~0.2 pp). For FY26, revenue grew 1.0% to INR246.05 bn, EBITDA was INR24.08 bn (9.8%) and PAT INR16.85 bn (6.8%). Management guided FY27 to mid-teen revenue growth and early double-digit EBITDA margins, citing April-May sell-through and recent price hikes.

financial_highlights.change: +8.1% YoY vs INR74.48 bn in Q4 FY25
Margin down ~250 bps YoY; up 7% sequentially

segments.name: Home Appliances & Air Solutions (H&A)
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 revenue INR65.16 bn (+5.7% YoY); FY26 revenue INR181.60 bn. EBIT margin 11.9% in Q4, hit by commodity costs, rupee depreciation and channel investments for new launches. Premium washers, French door refrigerators and 5-star RACs saw higher ASPs.

segments.name: Home Entertainment (HE)
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 revenue INR15.37 bn (+19.6% YoY, +15.9% QoQ); FY26 revenue INR64.44 bn. EBIT margin 13.4% in Q4, after time-bound Cricket World Cup marketing spend. OLED market share 60.0% YTD March 2026.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at mid-teen percentage; early double-digit EBITDA margin for full year, better than FY26.
Margin recovery levers: localization (55.2% in FY26, targeted +1 to 2 pp per year), operating leverage, richer mix, scaling AMC and B2B, export growth, and industry price increases.
Export expansion targeted 'very significantly' in FY27; large-capacity refrigerators exported to advanced markets from Q1 FY27; Essential Series exports to 22 countries.

Sri City plant: total investment INR50 bn, funded from internal accruals; compressor line Q3 FY27 (Oct-Dec 2026), RAC line Q4 FY27 (Jan-Mar 2027); washing machine and refrigerator lines to follow in phases.
Management expects ROE and ROCE to improve meaningfully in FY27 as profitability normalizes and Sri City capital starts generating returns.
No immediate plan for further price hikes; monitoring raw material and currency movements.
capex_capacity: Sri City (third factory) total planned investment INR50 bn; about INR6.57 bn deployed to March 2026 (CWIP and capital advances) (INR657 crore per Q&A). Next two years' spend largely planned against the INR5,000 crore total.
Sri City timelines: compressor production Q3 FY27; RAC production Q4 FY27; washing machine and refrigerator lines added thereafter in phases. Hiring for key roles has started.
Pune plant produces premium products: 674 litre and 790 litre side-by-side refrigerators, top freezers (790 litre plus) and front-load washing machines for export.
Sri City expected to double export-capable capacity and improve South India logistics (South India is 38-40% of business).
FY26 capex INR5.51 bn; localization rate 55.2%, up ~1.4 pp YoY.
demand_pricing: Channel: AC channel filled in Q4 (55% of annual AC business falls in Q4); >1 million ACs sold in Q4 FY26; industry entered Q1 FY27 with inventory at last year's levels, but March cold spell slowed sell-out. LG says its inventory was in line with plan and manageable.

Price hikes: RAC increased in two phases (BEE-rating driven, then input cost and FX), about 12-13% per analyst; refrigerators and washing machines also repriced. LG says competitive positioning unchanged and no impact on sales.

New categories: French door refrigerator share rose from 5% to 14% by March 2026 after December 2025 launch; chest freezer (market ~INR3,000 crore, five models coming); fixed-speed RAC entry; dishwashers doubled revenue in FY26 and rank #2.
Essential Series (launched 14 Oct 2025): about 100,000 washing machines sold in Q4 FY26; ~80,000 Essential refrigerators in Q4; ~20,000 sub-1-ton RACs (0.8 ton).
TV: 55-inch and above segment grew 47% and now 49% of business; TV revenue grew 20%+ in Q4.
AC penetration in India cited at ~13%; B2B order inflows from government, corporate and hospitality; ID division hit record quarterly sales.

qa_highlights.question: Why did revenue growth of 8% not translate into operating leverage and a YoY margin decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Atul Khanna said margin fell ~250 bps: channel promotion ~1.1 pp (temporary, to drive sell-out and partner confidence), currency depreciation ~1 pp, and e-waste compliance ~0.2 pp as recycling target rose from 60% to 70%. Price hikes, lower promotions and summer demand are expected to restore margins in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is LG doing differently from peers, and how will margins recover?
qa_highlights.answer: Dongmyung Seo cited export scaling, the recovering B2B business, AMC as a high-margin recurring stream, and new categories. Margin levers: exports (core growth engine), localization (55.2%), and a higher mix of AMC and B2B. Lower oil prices after Middle East stabilisation could also help.

qa_highlights.question: What is the channel inventory now versus the start of the year?
qa_highlights.answer: Gurpinder Singh said the AC industry entered Q1 FY27 with inventory at last year's levels, with dealers cautious after a slow March. LG's inventory was aligned with plan, and current high temperatures are easing channel pressure.

qa_highlights.question: Are price hikes enough to protect margins, and are more planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjay Chitkara said AC prices were raised in two calibrated phases and that LG was first to move, with competitors following. Similar hikes were made on refrigerators and washers with no volume impact. No immediate further hikes are planned, but the company is monitoring raw materials and FX.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex outlook for FY27 and the Sri City timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Atul Khanna confirmed the Sri City plant is on track: compressor line in Q3 FY27, RAC line in Q4 FY27, and washing machine and refrigerator lines later. About INR657 crore is spent to March 2026, with the full INR5,000 crore to be funded from internal accruals over the next two years.

qa_highlights.question: Does LG still target doubling exports, and what is the Essential Series response?
qa_highlights.answer: Atul Khanna reiterated a very significant export expansion, with premium products to developed markets from Pune and Sri City. Sanjay Chitkara said Essential Series sales were encouraging, with 100,000 washers and 80,000 refrigerators in Q4, and exports are going to 22 countries.

qa_highlights.question: What is the demand outlook for April-May 2026 and the industry growth comparison?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjay Chitkara said ACs are well supported by summer demand and the company expects good growth. He targets strong double-digit to mid-teen growth across all four categories in FY27, but gave no industry growth figures for April-May.

qa_highlights.question: Whether the new categories are for domestic or export use?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjay Chitkara said the new categories serve both: chest freezers (five models, market ~INR3,000 crore), fixed-speed RACs, and large refrigerators from Pune, which target new domestic business and global markets.

risks_watch: Rupee depreciation (~5.6% YoY in Q4) and commodity costs, with management noting currency and geopolitical (US-Iran, Middle East) risks to FY27 costs.
Whether promotional intensity falls and price hikes stick, which underpin the early double-digit EBITDA margin target.
Sri City execution: compressor line Q3 FY27 and RAC line Q4 FY27 timing, plus ramp-up of hiring.
AC channel inventory and sell-out after the weak March; dependence on summer heat.
Export ramp-up: management did not quantify the 'significant' export growth target in this call, though an earlier doubling guidance was referenced.
Return ratios (ROE, ROCE) moderated in FY26 due to high cash balance and H1 headwinds; improvement depends on Sri City returns.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the medium term and on FY27 margin recovery, but cautious on near-term cost pressures from FX, commodities and geopolitics. Management was specific on Sri City timelines and product launches, and vaguer on export quantification and the industry growth comparison for April-May.
key_quotes: Despite a challenging global environment, our sales grew by 8.1% in quarter 4 '26, which provided some operating leverage benefit.
The single largest contributor was our channel promotion investments, which impacted margins by approximately 1.1%.

I am pleased to confirm that our Sri City plant construction is fully on track as per our plan and we remain committed to our INR 5,000 crore investment roadmap, deployed in a phased manner over the next few years, funded entirely from our internal accruals.
So, our clear guidance is to expand our exports very significantly considering the Middle East situation so far.
For the washing machine alone, we have sold 1 lakh units. In Q4 FY'26 and the similar period we sold roughly 80,000 Essential Series refrigerators.

growth.why: Management guides FY27 mid-teen revenue growth and early double-digit EBITDA margin, backed by April-May sell-through, recent price hikes, and new categories, with Sri City compressor line (Q3 FY27) and RAC line (Q4 FY27) as capacity support, though no order or utilisation figures were given.
